Time to get hands-on! The goal of these exercises is that prepare-draw-flip-wait stops feeling like a recipe you follow and starts feeling like something you *do*. This afternoon these skills will turn into a real experiment.

Work in a new script, `playground.py`, and **run after every step**.

### Step 1: A window with your favourite colour

Open a window: any background colour you like (`'black'`, `'grey'`, `'pink'`, `'darkblue'`...). Hold it for two seconds, close cleanly.

:::: {.content-visible when-meta="show-solutions-s2"}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show the code"}
```python
from psychopy import visual, event, core

win = visual.Window(size=(1280, 720), fullscr=False,
                    color='darkblue', checkTiming=False)
win.flip()      # paint the background — no flip, no colour!
core.wait(2)
win.close()
core.quit()
```
:::

::::

:::: {.content-visible unless-meta="show-solutions-s2"}

::: {.callout-tip icon="false" title="🔒 Example code will be available here after the workshop"}

### Step 2: Your name in lights

Before the wait: show your own name, big, in a colour that pops against your background. Play with `height` (try 0.05 vs 0.2) and `color` until you like it.

:::: {.content-visible when-meta="show-solutions-s2"}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show the code"}
```python
name = visual.TextStim(win, text='Chris was here!',
                       color='orange', height=0.15)
name.draw()
win.flip()
core.wait(2)
```
:::

### Step 3: One picture, on your command

Replace the name with one of the rabbit images (pick any file from `stimuli/`), and make it stay until *you* press a key: participant-paced, not timed.

### Step 4: A two-screen sequence
Now chain them: your name for two seconds (computer-paced), *then* the picture until a keypress (you-paced), then close. One prepare-draw-flip-wait per screen.

:::: {.content-visible when-meta="show-solutions-s2"}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show the code"}

```python
from psychopy import visual, event, core

win = visual.Window(size=(1280, 720), fullscr=False,
                    color='darkblue', checkTiming=False)

name = visual.TextStim(win, text='Anna was here!',
                       color='orange', height=0.15)
name.draw()
win.flip()
core.wait(2)

pic = visual.ImageStim(win, image='stimuli/stimulus1_R.jpg')
pic.draw()
win.flip()
event.waitKeys()

win.close()
core.quit()
```
:::

::::

:::: {.content-visible unless-meta="show-solutions-s2"}

::: {.callout-tip icon="false" title="🔒 Example code will be available here after the workshop"}
:::

### Step 4: Slideshow

**Finished early?** Turn Step 4 into a *slideshow*: `glob` all the stimulus images and loop over them, each until a keypress: Chapter 5's list meeting Session 1's for-loop.

:::: {.content-visible when-meta="show-solutions-s2"}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show the code"}
```python
import glob

images = glob.glob('stimuli/stimulus*.jpg')

for image in images:
    pic = visual.ImageStim(win, image=image)
    pic.draw()
    win.flip()
    event.waitKeys()
```
:::
